summary.intent: Ship phase 69 (a large FUSE/WinFsp Rust integration + grant-root awareness feature) autonomously through the full post-execution loop: verify, secure, validate, simplify, SDK/desktop E2E gates, CodeRabbit review, PR creation, review resolution, and learnings extraction.
summary.outcome: PR #594 was shipped and merged to main after the orchestrator ran all gates, applied ~13 verified code fixes (including a CRITICAL read-after-write EIO bug and a cross-platform 'Decryption failed' bug caused by hex vs base64 file_iv encoding mismatch between the Rust mount and TS read chain), migrated a stale legacy test helper to node/v3, and got the full Desktop E2E matrix green on macOS/Linux/Windows with 0 unresolved review threads and 7 deferred todos filed.

repo: cipher-box's user-added hard gate: full 'Desktop E2E Tests' workflow (desktop-e2e.yml) must be dispatched via `gh workflow run "Desktop E2E Tests" --ref <branch>` (no inputs needed) and required green before merge — it's dispatch-gated so it doesn't run automatically on PRs.

This repo squash-merges PRs, so branch commit subjects never reach release-please post-merge — only the PR title (conventional, paren-free) and the pr-release-preview.js gate (which tolerates parens in descriptions and skips merge commits) actually matter; a `git filter-branch` reword of already-conventional commits is unnecessary busywork.

CodeRabbit CLI times out on full diffs >~100 files/24k lines; scope reviews with `--dir` per-crate (e.g., crates/sdk, crates/fuse, crates/core) to get real results, and expect free-tier rate limiting after several scoped runs.
clippy is not CI-gated in this repo; most clippy warnings are pre-existing or in the vendored `fuser` crate, not worth fixing during a ship pass.
`.planning/` is excluded from markdownlint in CI (but prettier still runs), so CodeRabbit nitpicks on `.planning/*-PLAN.md` table formatting are non-blocking.

NodeContent.file_iv must be base64-encoded on the wire (matching TS/web `@cipherbox/core` contract) — the Rust FUSE mount was encoding it as hex, which only self-consistently worked for the mount's own reads and broke every cross-client/SDK decrypt.

tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/bump-ipns-sequence.ts was missed during the 69-25 node/v3 verifier migration and still used the legacy folder model (`folder.metadata.children`), causing a Windows-only conflict-detection test failure.

The cross-language KAT vectors use a sample IV (`000102...0b`) that is coincidentally valid as both hex and base64, so they never would have caught the file_iv encoding mismatch — a todo was filed to pin a discriminating sample.

code.finding: `is_unresolved` predicate duplicated the enclosing `if cid.is_empty()` check, making it always true and the `pending_content` fallback at 587-599 unreachable — causing read-after-write EIO on locally-buffered files.
`file_iv` was hex-encoded (`iv_hex`) at publish time but the TS/web read chain (`packages/sdk-core/src/file/index.ts`) expects base64 — fixed to base64 to match the cross-language contract.

Own-resolve generation gate compares the stored floor against itself (floor-vs-floor, a no-op) by design — safe because the (seq, CID) pair is IPNS-signature-bound and AEAD generation-AAD binding catches forged records; adversarially confirmed as safe-by-design, not a bug.

Used legacy `loadVaultKeyBlob().rootFolderKey` / `folder.metadata.children` / `updateFolderMetadataAndPublish()` legacy model instead of node/v3 (`unsealNode`, `resolveIpnsRecord`), causing `undefined.length` crash on Windows; migrated to node/v3 mirroring `edit-filepointer.mts`.

workflow: When a heavy background agent stalls/dies mid-stream (e.g. security auditor), check what it already produced before re-spawning a slow multi-minute agent — often faster to synthesize the report yourself from already-gathered evidence (register, verified SCs, test results).

Spawn parallel adversarial-verification agents (each covering a distinct code region) to triage large batches of automated-review findings (CodeRabbit/Greptile) rather than blindly applying or blindly deferring — false positives were caught this way (e.g. a 'fix' that would have damaged a desync-sensitive write-generation path).
When a CI push races with a user's own concurrent push, check `git log`/divergence immediately rather than assuming clobber; GitHub can auto-merge cleanly and preserve both sets of commits.
Use `gh api` reads/writes even when `git push`/`git fetch` are sandbox-blocked; only the git network operations need sandbox disabled.

Root-causing a cross-language crypto bug benefits from bisecting which decrypt 'layer' fails (child-ref unseal vs node unseal vs content decrypt) using KAT-vector pinning to rule out already-covered layers.

friction: gsd-verify-work skill is designed for conversational/human UAT, not the autonomous goal-backward VERIFICATION.md generation this workflow needed — had to bypass the skill's UAT flow and manually drive the verifier agent instead.

Security auditor agent stalled mid-stream after ~7.5 minutes with an 'API Error: Response stalled mid-stream' and produced no output, requiring manual reconstruction of the SECURITY.md from already-gathered evidence.
CodeRabbit CLI timed out on the full 125-file/24k-line diff during summarizing, requiring a fallback to directory-scoped reviews.
CodeRabbit CLI free-tier rate-limited after several scoped review runs, blocking the apps/desktop scope from local review (had to rely on PR-level review instead).
Committing via the git helper repeatedly timed out (1Password SSH signing hang) reporting false-negative failures — had to verify with `git log --oneline -1` each time rather than retry.
zsh's `$status` is a read-only variable, causing a background poll script to fail with exit code 1 on first attempt.
GitHub GraphQL thread-reply/resolve mutations failed silently/intermittently (known API flakiness), requiring debug runs with visible errors and retry loops.
`gh api` log retrieval for a failing Linux desktop-e2e step came back empty initially (logs still flushing), requiring a fallback to the run archive.

Desktop E2E matrix took ~30-45 minutes per run and had to be re-dispatched 4 times across the session as fixes landed (initial run, post-69-14, post-file_iv-fix, post-bump-helper-fix), consuming significant wall-clock time.
